nodes.t: Arithmetic, units and estimation
Algebra: rearranging formulas, equations, logs
Geometry and trigonometry: radians, sine waves
Vectors, matrices and complex numbers
Calculus: derivatives, integrals, first-order ODEs
Statistics and fitting for noisy sensors
Control math: second-order ODEs, Laplace, eigenvalues
Vectors and coordinates: dot, cross, normalise (three.js)
Matrices and transformations: translate, rotate, scale, 4x4
Coordinate spaces and projection: model, view, projection
Rotations and quaternions: Euler, gimbal lock, slerp
Curves and interpolation: Bezier
LearnOpenGL: getting started through lighting
Measurement, units and error
Motion: velocity, acceleration, free fall
Forces: Newton's laws, friction, free-body diagrams
Energy, power and momentum
Rotation: torque, inertia, gears
Electricity and magnetism: charge, current, motors
Waves and heat: ultrasonics, temperature rise
First circuits: Ohm's law, breadboard, multimeter
Circuit analysis: Kirchhoff, dividers, Thevenin
Capacitors, inductors and AC: RC, impedance, filters
Semiconductors: diodes, BJT, MOSFET switches
Op-amps and power: regulators, ripple, decoupling
Digital: gates, ADC and DAC, sampling
PCB design in KiCad
Microcontroller basics: pins, clock, flashing code
Peripherals: GPIO, PWM, ADC, timers, interrupts
Protocols: UART, I2C, SPI, logic analyser
Firmware structure: state machines, FreeRTOS
Wireless and IoT: ESP32, MQTT dashboard

ladders.name: GSoC
ladders.src: GSoC 2027 Roadmap, Python + AI Track (phases -1 to 4). The C/C++ Systems Track targets GSoC 2028 and is not imported.

nodes.t: Phase -1: Git and GitHub properly: clone, branch, PR, resolve a merge conflict
nodes.tiny: Make a branch and push one small change

nodes.t: Phase -1: numpy and pandas basics
nodes.tiny: Create one array and one dataframe

nodes.t: Phase -1: build 3-5 small real projects (CLI tool, CSV script, API caller, data cleaner)
nodes.tiny: Pick the first project and write what it does in one line

nodes.t: Phase -1: read an open-source Python file of about 200 lines and explain every function
nodes.tiny: Pick one small file and read the first function

nodes.t: Phase 0: pick a primary org and a backup (PSF, NumFOCUS AiiDA/ArviZ, CVXPY). Checkpoint: if Phase -1 is not solid by November 2026, consider GSoC 2028
nodes.tiny: List 3 orgs and read their front page

nodes.t: Phase 0: read CONTRIBUTING and get the codebase building and running locally
nodes.tiny: Clone the repo

nodes.t: Phase 0: join the community chat, introduce yourself, skim the test suite
nodes.tiny: Join the chat and say hello

nodes.t: Phase 1: find 2-3 good first issues and comment on one
nodes.tiny: Open the good first issue list

nodes.t: Phase 1: submit your first PR and iterate on review feedback
nodes.tiny: Trace the code path for the issue

nodes.t: Phase 1: second, slightly harder PR (small feature or real bug)
nodes.tiny: Pick the issue and comment on it

nodes.t: Phase 2: confirm the org is in GSoC 2027, read its ideas list, shortlist 2-3 ideas, message a mentor
nodes.tiny: Open the GSoC org list and search for your org

nodes.t: Phase 3: draft the proposal (1,500-2,500 words with a week-by-week timeline)
nodes.tiny: Write the problem statement paragraph

nodes.t: Phase 3: mentor review, register on the GSoC site, submit 24-48 hours before the deadline
nodes.tiny: Send the draft to a mentor

nodes.t: Phase 4: keep contributing small PRs while results are pending
nodes.tiny: Check the issue tracker for one small fix
